exactAcceptance: Current supported claims, usable retained data, exact scopes and reviewer must be recorded before promoting reference coverage. No numerical tolerances invented.
scope: Shared simMOVE reference-media contract and actual editing component; all supported image/video provenance records can bind named movement/body/side/phase. Browser flow checked on male/female/neutral contexts with synthetic nonpatient source; generic image/video contract, route and project-library JSON verified by focused tests.
supportedClaims: Exported route/project JSON preserves source hash, original observations, fitting options, exact named context and reviewer declaration without embedding media bytes.
An explicit permitted-source companion retains original media bytes and metadata outside one browser; a fresh browser can restore it without detector inference or silently applying a new pose.
Wrong raw file, altered companion, mismatched context and corrupt local identity are rejected before replacement or attachment.
Permission remains an unverified user declaration. Undeclared media cannot be exported as a companion. Legacy route records remain readable and require exact source reattachment.
limits: This verifies access, retention and binding of source evidence, not its anatomical truth, measurement accuracy, suitability or license approval.
No existing motion receives clinical/reference qualification, Blender approval or native-dynamics acceptance from this feature. Movement and physics inputs are unchanged.

Existing catalogue closure gate requires unrelated whole-movement qualification. This property evidence is retained separately; the defect is not formally closed and the frozen milestone receives no closure count.
One media companion holds one source observation contract; a route may retain several contracts for frames from the same source. Users must explicitly retain/export their necessary companions.
Local source feature verified, not yet committed, merged or deployed.
